top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is one original, testable idea (cancelling light shifts so many neutral atoms can be interrogated on a narrow transition without Doppler or recoil shifts) that is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, has been reproduced across laboratories, and reached 10^-18 uncertainty. The two-name allocation maps onto two documented contributions, and a citation centred on many-atom lattice interrogation handles the attribution reservations. This is clearly preferable to no award.
